Maya (Product): uploaded a compact p95 card proposal to Figma https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE — can we decide hover content and keyboard behavior? Eli (Design): looked — love the condensed layout. quick concern: current hover panel covers the chart and hides the scrubber. prefer an overlay anchored to the right so users can still interact with the timeline. Sam (Frontend): overlay might break on narrow viewports. a sticky bottom popover could avoid overlap. also: pointer-only hover is not enough — keyboard focus must open the same panel. Kai (Eng): agree on keyboard. propose: `aria-describedby` for the trigger + `role=\"dialog\"` for the panel and `aria-live=\"polite\"` for incremental updates. tiny example: ```
p95 320ms (n=1,234)
``` Eli (Design): nice snippet. also color scale for the density map should be colorblind-safe — thinking Viridis or a ColorBrewer sequential scheme rather than the current red->yellow->green. Jordan (PM): keep the hover summary to one short sentence: "p95: 320ms — spike driven by bursty batch jobs" and then a link to drill into the query. shorter microcopy reduces clutter. a11y-bot: automated note: ensure three keyboard interactions for the panel: Enter/Space to open, Esc to close, Left/Right to move scrubber thumb. Add `aria-valuenow`/`aria-valuetext` on the scrubber element. Maya (Product): sampling controls question: should sampling rate be global (top-level) or per-card? leaning per-card so teams can tune noise per widget. Sam (Frontend): per-card gives more control but increases settings surface. alternative: per-card override that falls back to org default — hide advanced options in a gear menu. Eli (Design): microcopy draft for the gear tooltip: "Sampling rate (samples/sec) — lower to smooth noise, higher to see transient spikes" — too long? Jordan (PM): shorter: "Sampling rate — lower to reduce noise". keep it explicit and scannable. Kai (Eng): backend note: if we surface sample count ("n samples") in the hover we can help users assess confidence. cheap to add if instrumentation already emits it. Eli (Design): accessibility nit: current scrubber knob looks small in mock; hit target 44px and increase focus ring contrast. use a 3px outline with system focus color. also ensure the popover is announced on open. Maya (Product): last design decision: heatmap bucket count — 3 buckets for clarity vs 5 for nuance. which direction? Sam (Frontend): pragmatic: use 3 buckets on mobile (simpler legend) and 5 on desktop. switch by CSS breakpoint or compute server-side. Eli (Design): sounds good. I'll update the Figma file with: right-anchored overlay on desktop, sticky bottom popover on narrow screens, per-card sampling under gear, colorblind-safe palette, stronger focus styles, and the shortened microcopy. will ping when ready for a final pass. :thumbsup: Maya (Product): thanks — tagging follow-ups: @Eli to update mocks, @Sam/Kai to validate keyboard interactions, @Jordan for copy sign-off. I moved a small accessibility checklist into the figma comments. Sam (Frontend): quick implementation note — for the hover contents let's lazy-load details only after first open to keep initial render cheap. Eli (Design): updated figma (v2) pushed. see comment thread. will loop back after frontend validation. Maya (Product): perfect. ending thread — will merge decisions into the spec doc later.
